title: Baked Gruyère Mac and Cheese
description: Gruyère, sharp white cheddar, and Parmesan in a creamy sauce, baked under a crisp, buttery panko crust. You can put it together hours ahead and bake it when you need it.

items: 1 lb cavatappi or elbow macaroni
2 tbsp kosher salt, for the pasta water
3 cups whole milk
1 1/2 cups heavy cream
5 tbsp unsalted butter
1 shallot, finely minced (or 1/4 medium yellow onion)
2 garlic cloves, grated
5 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 oz cream cheese, softened
1 tbsp Dijon mustard
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
1 tsp kosher salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
8 oz Gruyère, grated (about 2 cups)
8 oz sharp white cheddar, grated (about 2 cups)
1 oz Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated (about 1/2 cup)
1 1/2 cups panko bread crumbs
3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
1 oz Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated (about 1/2 cup)
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
Pinch of kosher salt

Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish. Grate all the cheese from blocks. Pre-shredded cheese is coated with starch to keep it from clumping, and that coating makes the sauce grainy.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 2 tablespoons of salt. Cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the package's shortest time, then drain it. It will finish cooking in the oven.
Warm the milk and cream together in a saucepan or the microwave until steaming.
Melt the butter in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the shallot until soft, about 3 minutes (about 5 minutes if you're using onion), then add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, whisking constantly. Don't let it brown.
Slowly pour in the warm milk and cream, whisking as you go. Simmer, whisking often and scraping the corners of the pot, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon, 5 to 7 minutes.

Take the pot off the heat. Whisk in the cream cheese, mustard, nutmeg, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Add the Gruyère, cheddar, and 1/2 cup Parmesan a handful at a time, stirring until each handful melts before adding the next.
Taste the sauce. It should be a little saltier and a little thinner than you want the finished dish to be, because the pasta soaks up salt and liquid as it bakes.
Fold the pasta into the sauce and spread it in the baking dish.
Toss the panko with the melted butter, the remaining Parmesan, the thyme, and a pinch of salt. Scatter it evenly over the pasta.

Bake for about 25 minutes, until the sauce bubbles at the edges and the crumbs are deep golden. If the top is still pale, put it under the broiler for a minute or two and watch it closely, since panko burns fast.
Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving so the sauce thickens.

Assemble everything up to the point where the pasta goes into the dish, but keep the crumb topping separate. Cover the dish tightly. It can sit on the counter for up to 2 hours; otherwise refrigerate it for up to a day.
The pasta keeps soaking up sauce while it waits, so pour about 1/2 cup of milk evenly over the top before you add the crumbs.

If you bake it straight from the fridge, plan on 45 to 55 minutes. Cover it loosely with foil for the first 25 minutes so the crumbs don't brown before the middle is hot. If you let it sit out for 30 to 45 minutes first, 35 to 40 minutes uncovered is usually enough.
It's done when the sauce bubbles in the center as well as at the edges, or when the center reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Don't put a cold glass baking dish straight into a hot oven, or it can crack. Let it sit out for at least 30 minutes first.
